title: Hosted API: Multi-lane rollout PRD + Acceptance & Launch Checklist (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Define the product requirements, acceptance criteria, testing harness and step-by-step launch checklist for shipping a converged hosted inference surface covering chat, completions, embeddings and rerank. This ticket focuses on a multi-lane rollout model (latency-sensitive, cost-optimized, and fallback lanes) plus a synthetic acceptance harness to detect regressions by workload slice prior to progressive traffic shaping.
problem_statement: Customers need predictable behavioral and performance guarantees when migrating to the unified hosted surface. Historically, quality regressions and hidden latency/cost spikes occur only after broad launch. We must provide a deterministic acceptance path so that model, runtime, and shaping changes can be validated per-lane before ramping to production traffic.
goals: Define contract and behavioral surface for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints (stable request/response fields).
Create lane definitions: low-latency (SLO 150ms P95 gen token), balanced, and cost-optimized (quantized) lanes with clear mapping rules.
Deliver an automated acceptance harness that runs golden prompts + stratified synthetic load across lanes.
Ship a launch checklist for staged rollout with canary %, rollback criteria and telemetry dashboards.
non_goals: Not standardizing internal model weight compatibility—model adapters handled by research onboarding doc.
api_contract_summary: Unified endpoint family: /v1/inference/{mode} where mode in {chat, completion, embedding, rerank}. Requests include client_metadata, prompt/pair inputs, lane_hint optional header. Responses include output.tokens, structured.metadata.{latency, model_variant, quantization}, and quality_score when available. Backwards-compatible: v1 clients continue to function; new structured.metadata fields are additive.
lane_definitions: low-latency: pinned high-priority queue, higher cost model families, target P95 token time <= 150ms for typical 256-token sequences.
balanced: default lane for general traffic, target P95 <= 300ms for 256-token sequences, optimized batching enabled.
cost-optimized: quantized models and heavy batching allowed, target throughput for embeddings 10k/sec per GPU and best-effort latency.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: All endpoints respond with expected schema under smoke tests (chat/completion/embedding/rerank) and structured.metadata fields present.
Behavioral: Golden-prompt intent parity — top-1 intent match >= 98% vs baseline for chat; embedding cosine similarity mean >= 0.995 vs baseline embedding model on seeded corpus.
Performance: Per-lane latency SLOs met in synthetic profiles for 95th and 99th percentiles (thresholds documented in lane_definitions).
Cost: Cost-per-token for cost-optimized lane not exceed 0.8x current baseline when using suggested quantization profiles.
Stability: No increase in 5xx rate > 0.05% above baseline during a 30-minute full-suite acceptance run.
Safety: Safety filter throughput verified; no safety-rules false-positive increase > 1% on curated safety testset.
Operational: Telemetry emits per-request lane routing tag, model_variant, kernel_profile_id, and kv_cache_hit boolean; console dashboard populated and validated.
Security: SSO/Role-based access enforced for launch ops; audit logs present for production cutover events.
testing_plan: Acceptance harness: nightly synthetic suite combining golden-prompts, adversarial prompts, and regionally-distributed traffic emulation.
Load profiles: small (10rps), medium (200rps), canary (1% gradual increase to 10%), and soak (8 hours at expected peak) across lanes.
Quality regression detection: automated diff report (semantic and token-level) vs baseline with alerts on >1% regression signals.
Integration tests: End-to-end with SDKs (python/js), streaming and function-call paths verified.
Chaos tests: network partition, node preemption and kernel-fallback scenarios executed in a staging ring.
rollout_plan: Pre-launch: complete acceptance harness run in staging, sign-off from Eng, SRE, and Trust teams.
Phase 0 (Canary): 0.1% of production traffic for 1 hour -> verify 5xx, latency, quality metrics.
Phase 1: 1% traffic for 3 hours -> validate per-lane distributions and cost metrics.
Phase 2: 10% traffic for 12 hours -> monitor edge cases and multi-region failover.
Phase 3: 50% traffic for 24 hours -> readiness gate for GA.
GA: 100% rollout with ongoing monitoring and auto-rollback triggers enabled.
rollback_triggers: P95 latency > lane threshold for 10 minutes with underlying kernel-level errors.
Quality regression alerts: top-1 intent mismatch > 2% over a 1-hour window for chat endpoints.
Customer-facing errors (SEV2/SEV1) reported by support during canary window.
observability_requirements: Per-route dashboards: token-latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and model_variant breakdown.
Alerting: SLO burn rate alerts for each lane; anomaly detection for sudden quality metric drift.
Tracing: distributed traces must carry lane_hint and kernel_profile_id for root-cause analysis.
Retention: 30-day retention for request-level telemetry in staging; 90-day for production aggregated metrics.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hidden quality regressions when switching model_variant in cost-optimized lane. Mitigation: pairing quantized candidate with golden-prompt regression gates and canary only on background traffic first.
Risk: Increased tail latency under batching heuristics. Mitigation: introduce adaptive micro-batching cap and experiment toggle in runtime that can be switched off per-lane.
Risk: Telemetry gaps at high throughput. Mitigation: sampled request tracing plus synthetic probes and end-to-end e2e checks.
